raw.description:
The Senior Manager, Global Investigator Grants leads the global grants team responsible for processing investigator site payments through the Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS), ensuring payments are accurate, timely, and in accordance with the financial terms of the Clinical Trial Agreement. This role serves as the financial lead on project teams for site payments, providing oversight of payment processing, advance reconciliations, and month-end reporting. The position is heavily client facing, partnering directly with clients to review monthly investigator grant results, accruals, forecasting, and change order budgets.

As the Global Investigator Grants liaison with Business Operational Excellence, the Senior Manager will play a key role in the implementation of the CTMS Site Payment Module, including data validation, system setup, and the development of training materials, and will transition the team to processing site payments in the CTMS. This role is critical to strengthening process efficiency, internal controls, and the overall site payment experience for Precision, our clients, and investigator sites.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Serves as the financial lead on the Project Team for site payments on a global basis, ensuring investigator payments are processed through the CTMS in accordance with the financial terms of the Clinical Trial Agreement (CTA)
  • Leads the global grants team responsible for site payment processing in the CTMS, including, but not limited to: timely and accurate investigator payments, advance (pre-paid funds) balance reconciliations, and reporting
  • Serves as the Global Investigator Grants liaison with Business Operational Excellence for the implementation of the CTMS Site Payment Module, including data validation, system setup, and the development of training materials, and leads the team's transition to processing site payments in the CTMS
  • Oversees the setup and maintenance of site payment terms in the CTMS on a global basis, interpreting the financial section of the CTA to ensure payment schedules are configured accurately and payments are processed timely
  • Responsible for contributing to the month-end close process by generating a global report from the CTMS on a project-by-project basis inclusive of, but not limited to: amounts invoiced/paid, advance balances remaining, prepaid balance analysis, projections, and other key performance indicators as applicable
  • Works with the respective Project Directors and Project Managers to provide guidance on the financial section of the Clinical Trial Agreement
  • Works with the respective Project Directors and Project Managers to ensure visits and other payment-eligible activities are accurately captured in the CTMS so they can be tracked and paid; provides training as applicable
  • Ensures site payments processed in the CTMS meet the terms and conditions of the Clinical Trial Agreement, with appropriate review, approval, and internal controls
  • Responsible for overseeing the Sunshine Act Reporting process and other client reporting as applicable on a global basis, leveraging CTMS payment data
  • Serves in a heavily client-facing capacity, leading regular client meetings to review monthly investigator grant results, accruals, forecasting, and change order budgets; participates in internal team calls and Quarterly Business Review Meetings as applicable
  • Other duties as assigned by manager

Minimum Education and Experience:

  • Minimum of bachelor's degree in business administration, Accounting, Finance or similar field
  • Minimum of 5 years of CRO experience or equivalent relevant experience and/or demonstrated competencies in the key requirements of the role
  • Experience implementing the site payment module within a Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS), including data validation, system setup, and user training; experience with Veeva Vault CTMS preferred
  • Minimum of 3 years of managing direct reports

Knowledge, Skills, and Competencies:

  • Experience with clinical trial payment process, internationally
  • Experience with clinical trial agreements and site budgets
  • Strong understanding of the study start-up process
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Excellent time management skills
  • Analyze, reconcile, and communicate financial results with all levels of project team, investigator sites, and clients.

raw.description:
This is a limited duration role to cover for a leave of absence.


Position is eligible for remote work within the United States.

Summary

The Provider Documentation and Billing Auditor is responsible for conducting independent audits, reviews, and monitoring activities related to provider documentation, coding, billing, and reimbursement practices across the Mary Free Bed system. This role evaluates compliance with organizational policies and procedures, federal and state laws and regulations, payer requirements, and applicable coding and billing standards to help ensure the integrity of provider services and revenue cycle operations.


The Auditor assesses existing documentation, coding, and billing processes to identify compliance risks, control gaps, operational inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement. Through audit findings, data analysis, and collaboration with clinical, operational, and provider leaders, the Auditor develops recommendations to strengthen internal controls, enhance documentation accuracy, improve billing compliance, and support appropriate reimbursement.


A key responsibility of this position is to identify, investigate, correct, and help prevent documentation and billing issues through ongoing monitoring, education, and proactive compliance initiatives. The Auditor serves as a subject matter resource for providers, advanced practice providers, leadership, and staff regarding documentation integrity, coding accuracy, billing requirements, and regulatory expectations.


The Provider Documentation and Billing Auditor plays a critical role in promoting a culture of integrity, accountability, and compliance throughout the organization by fostering awareness of regulatory requirements and supporting continuous improvement efforts. This position reports directly to the Compliance Officer.

Essential Job Responsibilities

  • Conduct audits and reviews of provider documentation, coding, billing, and reimbursement practices to assess compliance with applicable laws, regulations, payer requirements, and organizational policies.
  • Evaluate the accuracy, completeness, and adequacy of clinical documentation to ensure services billed are supported by the medical record and meet coding, billing, and medical necessity requirements.
  • Perform ongoing monitoring activities to identify compliance risks, billing vulnerabilities, coding trends, and opportunities for process improvement.
  • Review provider and advanced practice provider documentation for adherence to federal and state regulations, Medicare and Medicaid requirements, commercial payer guidelines, and industry standards.
  • Identify potential overpayments, underpayments, coding inaccuracies, documentation deficiencies, and other compliance concerns, and recommend appropriate corrective actions.
  • Collaborate with compliance team, providers, advanced practice providers, revenue cycle staff, operational leaders, and other departments to resolve identified issues and improve compliance performance.
  • Provide education and training to providers and staff regarding documentation requirements, coding standards, billing regulations, compliance expectations, and best practices.
  • Serve as a subject matter resource on provider documentation integrity, coding, billing compliance, reimbursement requirements, and regulatory developments.
  • Assist in the development, review, and revision of policies, procedures, and internal controls related to provider documentation, coding, billing, and compliance activities.
  • Maintain thorough and accurate audit workpapers, documentation, reports, and records in accordance with compliance and departmental standards.
  • Assist in monitoring changes in healthcare laws, regulations, payer guidance, coding requirements, and industry best practices, and assess organizational impact.
  • Promote a culture of integrity, ethical conduct, accountability, and regulatory compliance throughout the Mary Free Bed system.

Perform other duties and special projects as assigned by the Compliance Officer.

Contribute by identifying problems and seeking solutions. Promote patient/family satisfaction where possible; participates in departmental efforts to monitor and report customer service.

Essential Job Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or higher in health information management, healthcare administration, nursing or related field.
  • Experience: 2-5 years of provider coding and billing experience in professional services.

Experience auditing:

  • Evaluation and Management (E/M) services
  • CPT coding
  • ICD-10-CM diagnosis coding
  • HCPCS Level II coding
  • Modifier usage
  • Medicare and commercial payer requirements
  • Documentation requirements supporting billed services

  • Advanced knowledge of compliance and auditing principles, theories and concepts
  • Auditing, Compliance, Healthcare billing and/or coding certification preferred.

  • Works independently and with minimal direction.

You will be the first point of contact for prospective customers across the medical and aesthetic markets.   • Plastic surgery groups and clinics

  • Follow up on unresponsive leads through calls, emails, and voicemails using a structured cadence.
  • Keep CRM records accurate and current, logging all activity, notes, and lead status.
  • Research target accounts to find new contacts and build prospect lists.
  • Meet or exceed weekly and monthly goals for calls, conversations, and qualified appointments.
  • Share market feedback, common objections, and competitor insights with the sales team.

Required

  • 3 to 5+ years of successful, verifiable experience in appointment setting, inside sales, telemarketing, lead generation, or a similar phone based role
  • Excellent verbal and written English communication skills, with a confident, professional phone presence and clear, easily understood speech
  • Proven ability to handle high call volume and stay motivated through rejection
  • Strong listening and questioning skills
  • Highly organized, self motivated, and able to work independently in a remote environment
  • Comfortable with CRM and ERP systems and Microsoft Office

Preferred

  • Experience selling or setting appointments in the medical device, surgical, healthcare, or aesthetics industries
  • Familiarity with hospital purchasing, GPOs, value analysis committees, or ASC operations
  • Understanding of B2B sales processes and buying decisions involving multiple stakeholders
  • Experience with sales engagement tools (e.g., Outreach, Salesloft, ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator)
  • Bachelor's degree

raw.description:
The Senior Manager, Global Investigator Grants leads the global grants team responsible for processing investigator site payments through the Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS), ensuring payments are accurate, timely, and in accordance with the financial terms of the Clinical Trial Agreement. This role serves as the financial lead on project teams for site payments, providing oversight of payment processing, advance reconciliations, and month-end reporting. The position is heavily client facing, partnering directly with clients to review monthly investigator grant results, accruals, forecasting, and change order budgets.

As the Global Investigator Grants liaison with Business Operational Excellence, the Senior Manager will play a key role in the implementation of the CTMS Site Payment Module, including data validation, system setup, and the development of training materials, and will transition the team to processing site payments in the CTMS. This role is critical to strengthening process efficiency, internal controls, and the overall site payment experience for Precision, our clients, and investigator sites.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Serves as the financial lead on the Project Team for site payments on a global basis, ensuring investigator payments are processed through the CTMS in accordance with the financial terms of the Clinical Trial Agreement (CTA)
  • Leads the global grants team responsible for site payment processing in the CTMS, including, but not limited to: timely and accurate investigator payments, advance (pre-paid funds) balance reconciliations, and reporting
  • Serves as the Global Investigator Grants liaison with Business Operational Excellence for the implementation of the CTMS Site Payment Module, including data validation, system setup, and the development of training materials, and leads the team's transition to processing site payments in the CTMS
  • Oversees the setup and maintenance of site payment terms in the CTMS on a global basis, interpreting the financial section of the CTA to ensure payment schedules are configured accurately and payments are processed timely
  • Responsible for contributing to the month-end close process by generating a global report from the CTMS on a project-by-project basis inclusive of, but not limited to: amounts invoiced/paid, advance balances remaining, prepaid balance analysis, projections, and other key performance indicators as applicable
  • Works with the respective Project Directors and Project Managers to provide guidance on the financial section of the Clinical Trial Agreement
  • Works with the respective Project Directors and Project Managers to ensure visits and other payment-eligible activities are accurately captured in the CTMS so they can be tracked and paid; provides training as applicable
  • Ensures site payments processed in the CTMS meet the terms and conditions of the Clinical Trial Agreement, with appropriate review, approval, and internal controls
  • Responsible for overseeing the Sunshine Act Reporting process and other client reporting as applicable on a global basis, leveraging CTMS payment data
  • Serves in a heavily client-facing capacity, leading regular client meetings to review monthly investigator grant results, accruals, forecasting, and change order budgets; participates in internal team calls and Quarterly Business Review Meetings as applicable
  • Other duties as assigned by manager

Minimum Education and Experience:

  • Minimum of bachelor's degree in business administration, Accounting, Finance or similar field
  • Minimum of 5 years of CRO experience or equivalent relevant experience and/or demonstrated competencies in the key requirements of the role
  • Experience implementing the site payment module within a Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS), including data validation, system setup, and user training; experience with Veeva Vault CTMS preferred
  • Minimum of 3 years of managing direct reports

Knowledge, Skills, and Competencies:

  • Experience with clinical trial payment process, internationally
  • Experience with clinical trial agreements and site budgets
  • Strong understanding of the study start-up process
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Excellent time management skills
  • Analyze, reconcile, and communicate financial results with all levels of project team, investigator sites, and clients.
  • Strong working knowledge of the grant administration and site contracting process on a global basis with the ability to thrive in a multi-tasking environment
  • Strong financial and analytical skills.
  • High energy and enthusiasm with a strong commitment to exceeding expectations.
  • Flexibility and willing to work on multiple assignments of varying tasks with personnel throughout the organization.
  • Ability to learn quickly in order to make an immediate impact and provide value-added services throughout the organization and with our clients.
  • Strong communication & interpersonal skills, displaying the ability to connect and build relationships with management and others throughout the organization.
  • Exhibits high self-motivation, and is able to work and plan independently as well as in a team environment.
  • Team player with a strong desire to be an active, long-term participant in the growth of the company.
  • Focuses on continuous improvement, including the ability to make proactive assessments on how to make processes more efficient while enhancing internal controls.

Position Summary

The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) – Retail Banking is responsible for establishing and leading the enterprise-wide risk management framework for the retail banking business. The CRO oversees credit, operational, market, liquidity, compliance, fraud, cyber, conduct, and reputational risks while ensuring alignment with the bank's strategic objectives, regulatory requirements, and risk appetite.

The role provides independent oversight and challenge to business activities, safeguarding the institution's financial stability, customers, and reputation while enabling sustainable growth.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Risk Management

  • Develop and maintain the retail banking risk management framework.
  • Establish risk appetite statements, risk limits, and governance standards.
  • Ensure effective identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation of risks.
  • Provide independent oversight of business decisions and strategic initiatives.
  • Promote a strong risk culture throughout the organization.

Credit Risk Management

  • Oversee retail credit portfolios, including:
    • Mortgages
    • Personal Loans
    • Credit Cards
    • Auto Loans
    • Consumer Finance Products
  • Establish underwriting standards and credit policies.
  • Monitor portfolio quality, delinquency trends, and loss performance.
  • Lead stress testing and credit risk scenario analyses.
  • Recommend risk-adjusted lending strategies.

Operational Risk Management

  • Develop frameworks to identify and manage operational risks.
  • Monitor operational incidents, control failures, and emerging risks.
  • Oversee business continuity and operational resilience programs.
  • Strengthen internal controls and risk reporting mechanisms.
  • Ensure effective risk and control self-assessment processes.

Regulatory Compliance & Conduct Risk

  • Ensure compliance with banking regulations and consumer protection laws.
  • Oversee conduct risk management and fair customer treatment initiatives.
  • Maintain strong relationships with regulatory authorities.
  • Lead regulatory examinations and risk-related audits.
  • Ensure implementation of regulatory changes and risk controls.

Fraud & Financial Crime Risk

  • Oversee fraud prevention, detection, and investigation programs.
  • Strengthen anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing controls.
  • Monitor financial crime risks and emerging threats.
  • Ensure effective transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting.
  • Collaborate with law enforcement and regulatory agencies when necessary.

Market & Liquidity Risk Oversight

  • Monitor interest rate risk and liquidity risk exposures.
  • Evaluate balance sheet vulnerabilities and stress scenarios.
  • Support asset-liability management activities.
  • Ensure adherence to regulatory capital and liquidity requirements.

Cybersecurity & Technology Risk

  • Oversee technology and cyber risk governance.
  • Assess cybersecurity threats and resilience capabilities.
  • Ensure robust controls for digital banking platforms.
  • Monitor third-party and vendor risk exposures.
  • Support digital transformation initiatives through effective risk management.

Governance & Reporting

  • Present risk reports to Executive Management, Risk Committees, and the Board.
  • Develop key risk indicators (KRIs) and risk dashboards.
  • Ensure timely escalation of significant risk issues.
  • Maintain effective risk governance structures and committee frameworks.

Leadership & Talent Development

  • Lead risk management teams across multiple disciplines.
  • Develop future risk leaders and succession plans.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, integrity, and transparency.
  • Promote collaboration across business, compliance, audit, and technology functions.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business Administration, Risk Management, Mathematics, or a related discipline.
  • Master's degree (MBA, Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or related field) preferred.

Professional Certifications

Preferred certifications include:

  • Financial Risk Manager (FRM)
  • Professional Risk Manager (PRM)
  • Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)
  • Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS)

Experience

  • 15+ years of progressive banking and risk management experience.
  • Extensive experience within retail banking risk management.
  • Proven leadership experience overseeing enterprise risk functions.
  • Experience interacting with regulators, boards, and executive committees.
  • Strong understanding of consumer lending, deposits, payments, and digital banking.
  • Experience leading large, multidisciplinary risk teams.

Technical Competencies

raw.description:
Nomios' mission is to build a 'secure and connected' future. Organisations across Europe depend on us to help secure and connect their digital infrastructures. In support of our continued UK growth, we are seeking an experienced SOC Analyst to join our 24/7 Security Operations Centre. Candidates must have previous hands-on SOC experience, with a strong preference for experience gained within a managed service provider (MSP) or managed security service provider (MSSP) supporting multiple customer environments.

Please note: this role has a planned start date of January 2027. We welcome applications from candidates who can commence employment at that time.

You will be working across a diverse set of customer environments as part of our Security Operations Centre, focusing on investigation, understanding attacker behaviour and contributing to the continual improvement of SOC capabilities.

Your role as Security Operations Centre (SOC) Analyst

As a 24/7 SOC Analyst, you will be on the frontline of our Security Operations Centre, monitoring, investigating and escalating security events across multiple customer environments. You will apply established SOC experience from day one, work confidently within customer-specific workflows and service commitments, and collaborate with Senior and Lead Analysts on complex investigations. You will use platforms including Microsoft Sentinel and Defender, Palo Alto Networks XSIAM, XDR and XSOAR, SentinelOne, CrowdStrike Falcon and Google SecOps to establish what happened, how activity progressed and what action is required.

You will join a modern, continuously evolving SOC run by people who are technical at heart and understand what analysts need to succeed. Career development is a core focus, with clear pathways into Threat Intelligence, SOC Engineering, SOC Professional Services, senior SOC roles and Incident Response for those who want to specialise. You’ll be part of a collaborative, agile team that values curiosity, humour and a genuine interest in technology. The environment is built around continuous improvement, with everyone having a voice in shaping how the department evolves. Regular team events and knowledge-sharing sessions create a supportive, engaging place to work.

Key Responsibilities

Detect and investigate

  • Monitor and triage alerts across SIEM, EDR or XDR, email and web security platforms.

  • Investigate suspicious activity and determine whether escalation is required.

  • Follow SOC runbooks and investigation workflows.

  • Build clear timelines of activity and maintain accurate investigation notes.

  • Escalate complex cases to Senior and Lead Analysts with appropriate context.

  • Review vulnerability management output and provide basic prioritisation insight.

Hunt and improve

  • Take part in directed threat hunting activities.

  • Suggest improvements to detections, dashboards and runbooks.

  • Support testing of new use cases and detection logic.

Collaborate and communicate

  • Provide clear written updates for customers and internal stakeholders.

  • Participate in shift handovers to maintain continuity.

  • Work closely with Senior and Lead Analysts to develop your skills and technical depth.

Requirements

We hire result-orientated, smart, and high-energy individuals who bring a can-do attitude and a willingness to go the extra mile and deliver exceptional outcomes. You should be organised and rigorous, with excellent analytical skills. Good communication with internal stakeholders is vital, as is the ability to work as part of a dynamic team.

Required skills:

  • Previous hands-on experience working in a Security Operations Centre. This role is not suitable for candidates seeking their first SOC Analyst position.

  • For candidates from an MSP or MSSP background, a minimum of one year's hands-on experience using comparable SOC technologies and supporting multiple customer environments.

  • Experience triaging, investigating and escalating security alerts across SIEM, EDR or XDR platforms.

  • Strong understanding of attacker behaviours, TTPs and common malware execution chains, including phishing leading to script or binary execution.

  • Ability to identify indicators of compromise, build clear investigation timelines and distinguish legitimate administrative activity from suspicious behaviour.

  • Ability to read and interpret Windows event logs, authentication logs, process trees, network telemetry and other relevant log sources.

  • Understanding of core network protocols including DNS, HTTP, SMB and LDAP, together with operational knowledge of Windows, macOS and Linux.

  • Working knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK and experience applying it during investigations or detection development.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide accurate customer updates, investigation notes and shift handovers.

  • Strong Microsoft 365 skills, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint, plus experience of Salesforce or a comparable case-management platform.

Desirable skills:

  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Sentinel and Defender; Palo Alto Networks XSIAM, XDR and XSOAR; SentinelOne; CrowdStrike Falcon; or Google SecOps.

  • Experience using VirusTotal, ANY.RUN, Shodan, Qevlar, Vectra AI, Tracebit or Thinkst Canary as part of investigations, threat hunting or security validation.

  • Ability to query in KQL, CQL, S1QL, XQL or similar languages, and to improve detections, dashboards, runbooks or detection logic.

  • Hands-on technical certifications, particularly those assessed through practical labs or examinations rather than solely through multiple-choice testing.

  • A relevant degree in cyber security, digital forensics, incident response, networking, information technology, computing or programming.

  • Practical AI experience beyond browser-based prompting, such as building agents or agentic workflows; working with VS Code, Codex, Claude Code or Cowork; or using Copilot, Claude or ChatGPT for threat hunting, detection-rule creation and detection-as-code workflows through GitHub or GitLab.

  • Scripting or programming experience that supports investigation, automation, enrichment or detection engineering.

Job Specifics

  • Location: This role is home-based with occasional visits to the office in Basingstoke

  • Hours: 12-hour shifts: 2 days, 2 nights; 4 days/nights off. Flexibility with hours will be required in the event of a major incident

  • Security clearance: Eligibility for SC clearance (lived in the UK for five years consecutively) required. DV clearance eligibility is advantageous.

  • Start date: January 2027

Why would you choose to come and work with us?

We invest in our people. You will get to work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment where you are free to use your initiative in support of our strategic objectives. You will work alongside high calibre sales, technical, and operational experts as part of a supportive, tight-knit team, within which every individual has an important part to play and makes a real difference. Nomios offers a highly competitive salary and commission scheme along with industry-leading benefits.

Ready to make an impact? Apply now!


Nomios is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating and sustaining an environment in which everyone is provided with an equal opportunity to grow and develop, and no individual will be unjustly discriminated against. This includes, but is not limited to, discrimination because of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion and belief, sex and sexual orientation.

raw.excerpt: PRECISION AQ, the top payer marketing agency, supports global pharmaceutical and life sciences clients in the achievement of commercial excellence.
raw.description:
PRECISION AQ, the top payer marketing agency, supports global pharmaceutical and life sciences clients in the achievement of commercial excellence. We excel at demonstrating the economic, clinical, and societal value of creative medical treatments to payers, providers, patients, and policymakers. As leaders in the generation, analysis, and communication of that evidence, we are improving market access and supporting our clients in their mission of improving care for patients around the world.

The Director, Medical Writing is responsible for leading content development for multiple projects and providing input on strategy while working cross-functionally and with a high level of independence. The Medical Director is responsible for ensuring high quality regarding content, organization, clarity, accuracy, format, consistency, and adherence to regulatory and internal guidelines, styles, and processes.

Essential functions of the job include but are not limited to:

  • Independently develop strategic, high-quality, and medically accurate content for a wide range of medical communications resources for a medium-sized book of business (generally 3 – 4 assigned accounts but varies based on size) which span multiple therapeutic areas
  • Collaborate with internal team members to create compelling content that meets client objectives
  • Review project briefs and timelines, assign staff, and attend all kick-off meetings
  • Review content for scientific accuracy and appropriateness to the project
  • Ensure best practices for content development are followed and advise on strategic or client considerations
  • Liaise directly with client on strategy and content-related subject matter including medical, legal, regulatory review meetings
  • Discuss medical content with external stakeholders including medical professionals, key opinion leaders, and managed care customers as required
  • Plan and allocate resources based on business needs in conjunction with other internal stakeholders
  • Supervise 2 – 4 medical writers and/or scientific associates directly
  • Establish and track individual personal development plans for each team member and provide timely feedback
  • Assist in development of new business proposals including target product profiles (TPPs) and/or competitive analyses
  • Attend and present at business pitch meetings as needed
  • Promote and adhere to Precision Value and Health’s workplace values known as PRECISION Principles (Client Service, Purpose, Accountability, Mutual Respect and Collaboration)

Required Education:

  • BA/BS in life sciences
  • BA/BS in English combined with experience in a pharmaceutical agency, medical communications company or healthcare advertising

Required Experience:

  • 5 – 7 years of experience in the medical communication, pharmaceutical and/or healthcare industry

Required Skills:

  • Command of American Medical Association (AMA) style
  • Strong proficiency with Word, PowerPoint, and Adobe Acrobat
  • Strong proficiency with scientific search engines including PubMed and Google Scholar

Required Competencies:

  • Strong written and verbal communication
  • High analytic ability
  • Strong self-management, organizational, and time management
  • Ability to translate complex scientific concepts for a variety of managed care audiences
  • Ability to prioritize deadline-sensitive projects and juggle competing client priorities
  • Highly team- and detail-oriented

Preferred Education:

  • Advanced degree in life sciences (PharmD or PhD)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Expertise in gathering, evaluating, and summarizing healthcare business and scientific literature and insights data for a variety of managed care audiences
  • Working knowledge of managed markets, healthcare, and the healthcare delivery system; health reform legislation; and/or managed care experience (HMO, MCO, PBM, etc.)
  • Ability to develop engaging promotional content
  • Managed care experience
Precision is required by law in some states or cities to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This compensation range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to: skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Precision, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. This role is also eligible for a discretionary annual bonus, health insurance, retirement savings benefits, life insurance and disability benefits, parental leave, and paid time off for sick leave and vacation, among other benefits.

raw.description:
Overview

As a Senior Procurement Lead at Linesight, you will work with highly experienced, culturally diverse, and passionate teams nurturing a strong social dynamic and a shared sense of achievement. You will gain vast industry experience that will open doors for you, extend your skillset and expand your perspective. We will empower, support, and enable you to take real responsibility in your role so that you can take charge of your career progression with us. For us lasting trusted relationships are everything, both with our teams and our clients.

The Opportunity

In this role you will:

  • Develop, implement, and manage equipment sourcing strategies, from identification of supply chain partners through to receipt of materials on site, including expediting of orders, with a clear focus on the OFCI demands and pace of construction-led project delivery

  • Act as a strategic partner and maintain alignment with business partners, including client technical teams, construction managers and consultancy stakeholders, to ensure ongoing support of the agreed strategies

  • Lead the decision-making process and make recommendations on awards based on your expert market knowledge, particularly within construction and capital project environments

  • Own the evaluation of bids to determine the best overall value, reviewing quotations and proposals against specifications and terms and conditions, ensuring they align with construction sequencing and site requirements

  • Manage various bid requests and contract developments with rigorous attention to detail, partnering with legal and finance teams when needed, and ensuring all documentation reflects construction best practice

  • Develop statements of work, performance terms and Service Level Agreements for the project, tailored to construction-phase expectations and contractor deliverables

  • Utilise client-specific procurement systems and processes as required, ensuring compliance with all stage-gate approvals

  • Review procurement practices on an ongoing basis to ensure compliance with relevant laws, industry standards and construction-specific regulatory frameworks

  • Use your expert knowledge to identify and drive innovation in the procurement and supply chain process, with a focus on improving efficiency and delivery performance across OFCI construction packages

We would love to hear from you if you:

  • Have grown your procurement experience over the last 10 years with increasing levels of leadership

  • Have demonstrable experience in OFCI construction procurement package ideally within a consultancy environment, or experience in a construction setting within the pharmaceutical/medical device sectors, or from an EPC background in the oil and gas sector

  • Have a degree in a procurement or supply chain management related discipline

  • Have a CIPS certification or are on the path to complete it – we can support your progression

  • Have strong problem-solving skills and a commercial mindset to build balanced solutions and recommendations

  • Thrive on building positive relationships with your team and clients through a shared purpose and sense of openness and fun

  • Are an excellent communicator both verbally and in writing

About us

Linesight is a highly successful global project and cost management consultancy that keeps clients coming back. And for that we have our people to thank. You see we’re not like the others. We’re different. Unique. It’s our fresh thinking and focus on what matters that has led to our evolving. We are on a journey working in some of the most exciting innovative sectors with some of the world’s most prestigious companies delivering major projects that deliver a more sustainable built environment. We have an open culture and a flat structure where you can expect to be treated with genuine care, respect, and empathy. With Linesight, you can truly discover the power of team!

Diversity, inclusion and accessibility

Linesight is committed to transparent, equal opportunity employment practices. We are building a diverse and inclusive organisation, accessible to all, based on having a safe culture which enables all our people to be their true selves. We are a people business, and we understand that the more inclusive we are, the happier our people and better our work will be. We will ensure that individuals with disability are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or recruitment process and are accommodated in the workplace. If you require assistance or accommodation of any kind, please mention this in your application, we would love to hear from you!

raw.description:
Opportunity Type:

Regular

Summary:

The Senior Corporate Development Officer, Cause Marketing plays a key role in driving revenue through strategic cause marketing partnerships. This position is responsible for identifying, securing, and cultivating new national and global cause marketing partnerships, while also stewarding and expanding existing relationships to deepen engagement and grow support of HFHI's mission.

The Sr. CDO will collaborate closely with development leadership and key HFHI program stakeholders to maximize fundraising opportunities with Fortune 500 companies and other major corporations primarily in support of Habitat's Global Impact Fund. The Sr. CDO will manage a diverse pipeline and portfolio of prospects, including national and multi-national corporations and national media/PR agencies. The Sr. CDO will be responsible for achieving a revenue goal of $7-10 million annually.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Planning (25%)

  • Implement tools and strategies to increase partner engagement in cause marketing initiatives and other sources of unrestricted revenue, including leveraging partners’ employee and customer spheres of influence to fundraise on behalf of HFHI.
    • Partner with HFHI Marketing and Communications, key Resource Development teams and other organizational stakeholders to identify opportunities to collaborate to unveil new cause marketing prospects and opportunities.
    • Develop a comprehensive partner centric partnership strategy tailored to partners’ business goals and objectives in alignment with HFHI’s mission.
    • Identify partnership-specific strategies that deepen partner engagement with Habitat and foster mutually-beneficial, sustainable, mission-centered aligned partnerships.
    • Stay current on consumer trends, and best practices in cause marketing, retail, digital and corporate sponsorship; convert insights into actionable programs and new revenue streams. Define account-specific strategies that deepen partner engagement with Habitat and foster mutually-beneficial, sustainable, mission-centered partnerships.
    • Identify strategies to best collaborate with Habitat local affiliates/offices to unveil partnership opportunities.

Prospect Management and Solicitation (20%)
• Maintain an active pipeline of qualified prospects through systematic and ongoing research and outreach activities; qualify prospects; develop and present compelling comprehensive solicitation plans; ensure a diverse partner portfolio across industries to support long-term growth.
• Collaborate with HFHI leadership to develop relationships with key stakeholders at multiple levels across partner organizations.
• Develop and deliver creative and powerful presentations and proposals for corporate partnership opportunities; ensure organizational leadership involved in pitch are briefed and prepared for meetings.
• Negotiate partnership terms in collaboration with HFHI’s legal, finance, and communication teams to ensure compliance and mutual benefit.
• Work in collaboration with Habitat local affiliates/offices to cultivate opportunities for national partnership.
• Act as cause marketing subject matter expert and drive collaboration with other Corporate Development Officers to deepen and expand partnership opportunities.
• Steward existing Workplace Giving partners toward higher levels of contribution and integrate Workplace Giving into existing partnerships to maximize giving potential

Partner Stewardship (20%)

  • Serve as the primary relationship manager and design effective partnership programs for a portfolio of corporate partners, with a focus on long-term growth and increased impact.
    • Ensure 100% partner satisfaction through thoughtful stewardship and best-in-class customer service.
    • Maintain and expand base of corporate partner relationships through on-going communication and solicitation as appropriate; ensure timely renewals and continued partnership growth year-over-year, particularly as it pertains to support of the Global Impact Fund.
    • Leverage opportunities for high-touch stewardship such as invitations to HFHI events and executive-led volunteer experiences, customized stewardship reports, etc.

Collaboration (20%)

  • Collaborate with Resource Development peers in structuring/managing/growing cause marketing for national and multi-national partnerships.
    • Establish strong relationships with HFH affiliate Executive Directors and resource development teams as well as HFHI regional staff; support the collaborative development efforts among Habitat for Humanity entities including the identification of opportunities to share prospects with HFHI resource development colleagues and local Habitat affiliates, as appropriate. Consistent and ongoing collaboration with Habitat local affiliates/offices to unveil partnership opportunities and to fulfill partnership benefits that are executed through affiliates.

Administration, Reporting & Analysis (15%)
• Use systems for metrics tracking, analytics, and knowledge sharing, providing accurate activity and pipeline reports including revenue and expense forecasts as required.
• Provide timely partnership wrap up reports.
• Maintain current prospect and partner records in donor management system

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience.
    • 5+ years of experience in cause marketing, sales, fundraising, and/or prospect development.
    • Experience in securing complex, six- and seven-figure multi-year commitments from Fortune 500 companies.
    • Experience with international partnership strategy and development.
    • Ability to understand Fortune 500 company goals, prepare presentations/proposals that are mutually beneficial and experience in securing complex, six-and seven-figure multiyear commitments.
    • Outstanding oral and written communication skills with excellent interpersonal, presentation, and negotiation skills.
    • Working knowledge of principles of corporate social responsibility, cause marketing, employee engagement and sponsorship.
    • Solid understanding of cause marketing best practices, and BBB guidelines.
    • Experience with international partnership strategy and development.
    • Highly collaborative with winning relationship skills to build internal and external partnerships.
    • Creative, quick thinker who thrives in brainstorm sessions and who can think past obstacles to achieve a bigger vision.
    • Highly proactive and autonomous, capable of driving projects through in a complex and layered organization.
    • Solution-oriented with commitment to delivering excellent internal and external customer service.
    • Ability to complete multiple projects concurrently while balancing competing priorities; ability to meet deadlines.
    • Superior skills in project management, metrics, analytics and reporting.
    • Ability to effectively manage resources including travel expenses.
    • Computer literate; able to use word-processing, spreadsheet, database and project software.
    • Complex problem solving.

    PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS
    • Working knowledge and/or of principles of corporate social responsibility, sales, cause marketing, marketing and/or public relations.
    • Working knowledge of constituent management platforms such as Blackbaud CRM.
    • Knowledge of and passion for Habitat's worldwide mission.
    • Shopper marketing experience.

• Workplace giving experience.


Culture and Values

At Habitat for Humanity International, you join a community that believes in:
*Humility: We are part of something bigger than ourselves.
*Courage: We do what is right, even when it is difficult.
*Accountability: We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission.
*Safeguarding: We protect the rights, dignity, and safety of all people we serve and work alongside.

Hiring Range:

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

About Us:

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

raw.excerpt: Who we areDigiCert is a global leader in intelligent trust.
raw.description:
Who we are

DigiCert is a global leader in intelligent trust. We protect the digital world by ensuring the security, privacy, and authenticity of every interaction. Our AI-powered DigiCert ONE platform unifies PKI, DNS, and certificate lifecycle management, to secure infrastructure, software, devices, messages, AI content and agents. Learn why more than 100,000 organizations, including 90% of the Fortune 500, choose DigiCert to stop today’s threats and prepare for a quantum-safe future at

Job summary

Forward Deployed Engineers at DigiCert are software engineers who embed with a business function (Sales, Support, Finance, Legal, HR, Procurement, Marketing), learn how the work actually gets done, and ship production AI solutions that drive measurable efficiency and ROI: agents on our systems of record, automated workflows, and AI-native tools wired into the architecture people already use.

You are the hands-on CTO of each engagement. You’ll find where AI delivers the highest return, decide the technical plan, write and deploy the code, and keep improving it after launch.

This is not a research role. You will own the work from first conversation to production, and are judged on what ships and what it returns, not on pilots or demos.

What you will do

  • Embed and find the work.Sit with business users, understand and maptheir workflows, data, and systems, and find where AI accelerates growth or saves the most time and money.
  • Own the architecture.Decide whether to build, buy, or configure solutions, weighing cost, speed, and long-term fit, and lead the technical side of vendor evaluations.
  • Write and ship production code.Build integrations, agents, and workflows with retrieval, tool use, and human-in-the-loop review. Test, deploy, and support what you ship.
  • Make AI reliable.Build systems that hold up against fragmented data and unpredictable model behavior. Find the failure cases before users do and decide where humans stay in control.
  • Build the shared foundation.Partner with IT, Security, and Engineering on model access, identity and permissions, data connectivity, observability, and evaluation. Turn one-off wins into reusable components, so each engagement ships faster than the last.
  • Prove the value.Every solution ships with a baseline, a measured improvement, and a hard number (hours saved, cost avoided, cycle time cut) for the sponsoring executive.
  • Leave the business stronger.Work with our enablement team to train operators and power users, so systems keep running and improving after you move on.

How we work

The Enterprise AI team is intense by design. It's a small team with an outsized impact on the business: what we ship changes how DigiCert runs, and the results reach the top of the company. The pace is fast and the standards are high, but so is the support. People share what they learn, challenge each other, and step in to help.

This is probably not the right place if you want a narrow scope, a predictable pace, or distance from internal customers. This role is built for engineers who want ownership, hard problems, a steep learning curve, and work that visibly moves the business.

What you will have

  • 4+ years building and shipping production software that people depended on, and supporting it after launch. Software engineering, forward-deployed engineering, solutions engineering, or startup backgrounds all fit.
  • 2+ years building with LLMs in production: agents, retrieval, tool calling (including MCP), and context engineering. You can explain how you measured and improved a system’s performance, and what it was worth to the business.
  • Strong coding ability in Python or TypeScript/JavaScript. You write, test, review, and deploy your own code, and you are fluent with APIs, webhooks, data pipelines, and authentication (OAuth, SSO, role-based access).
  • Daily use of coding agents, and the discipline to review and validate what they produce.
  • Comfort and proficiency working directly with non-technical users: asking great questions, learning an unfamiliar business fast, and turning messy processes into working software.
  • Judgment in security and compliance-sensitive environments. You know what data cannot leave the building and design accordingly.
  • Clear and effective written and spoken communication. You can write a one-page memo that makes the technical and business case to an executive.

Nice to have

  • Prior forward-deployed engineering, product management, or early-engineer experience.
  • Experience integrating enterprise platforms such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, NetSuite, Jira, and Databricks.
  • Exposure to SOX, FedRAMP, or similar control environments.
  • Experience in a security or PKI company, or another business where trust is the product.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation and comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage
  • Retirement savings programs with company matching (401(k) or RRSP)
  • Generous paid time off, including holidays, and vacation
  • Paid parental leave and family support benefits
  • Life and disabilitycoverage
  • Flexible spending and health savings options (where applicable)
  • Health and wellness support, including gym reimbursement and wellness programs
  • Employee Assistance Program with 24/7confidential support for employees and families
  • Education assistance and professional development opportunities
  • Access to LinkedIn Learning and continuous learning resources
  • Employee referral bonus program and additional company perks and discounts
  • Internal rewards and recognition platform (Motivosity) to celebrate and acknowledge project wins, milestone achievements, and the outstanding contributions of our colleagues
  • Business travel insurance and global employee support programs

raw.description:
We're the team iGaming operators turn to when growth matters most — and we're growing fast ourselves. At Receptional, you'll find colleagues who are bright, ambitious, and genuinely supportive. Specialists who do their best work together, sharing ideas, moving fast, and holding themselves to a high bar.

Whether you're starting out or stepping up, you'll get genuine investment in your development through our internal academy, real variety in your work, and a direct impact on some of the biggest names in the industry. Competitive benefits, flexible working, and a team that has your back.

We were named Marketing Services Supplier of the Year at the EGR B2B Awards 2026, and Best Medium Agency to Work For at the Company Culture Awards 2025 — recognition for the work we do and the place we've built to do it.

Paid search in iGaming demands a level of precision and compliance awareness you won't find in most agency environments. The budgets are significant, the regulatory requirements are strict, and clients expect a manager who can own their accounts with genuine autonomy — not someone who needs constant oversight.

As a Paid Search Manager at Receptional you'll be running Google Ads and Microsoft Ads campaigns across a portfolio of iGaming clients, owning compliance for your accounts, managing up to two direct reports, and working closely with the Senior Paid Search Manager on strategy and client development. It's a specialist role with real ownership, clear progression, and the kind of technically demanding work that keeps experienced paid search professionals genuinely engaged.

What We're Looking For


You'll need to be a strong practitioner who can operate with genuine autonomy — someone who owns their accounts, spots issues before clients do, and brings strategic thinking to every campaign they touch. iGaming adds a compliance layer that not every paid search professional has experience with, but if you're thorough, detail-oriented, and take regulatory standards seriously, we'll get you up to speed. You'll also be managing direct reports, so clear direction, honest feedback, and genuine investment in people development comes with the territory.

Essential:
  • 3+ years' experience in Paid Search advertising, preferably agency-side
  • Strong hands-on experience with Google Ads — Search, Display, and Performance Max
  • Google Ads certified — current and maintained
  • Ability to manage client relationships independently — you prepare and deliver presentations with confidence
  • Good campaign planning capabilities — budgeting, forecasting, and performance management across multiple accounts
  • Willingness to line manage and develop junior team members
  • Able to work autonomously and manage competing priorities without things slipping
  • Numerate and analytically strong with clear verbal and written communication skills
  • Comfortable using AI tools to improve campaign efficiency and automate repeatable processes

Desirable:
  • Microsoft Advertising certified or actively working towards it
  • Experience managing Paid Social campaigns or working knowledge of Meta Ads
  • Familiarity with GA4, Looker Studio, or equivalent reporting tools
  • Experience contributing to agency partner relationships with Google or Microsoft
  • iGaming or regulated-sector experience — we'll get you up to speed if not

How you'll be measured
Campaign performance against agreed client KPIs, accuracy of spend management and budget forecasting, quality and timeliness of client reporting, iGaming compliance standards maintained independently across all accounts, direct report development progress, and deadline adherence across all deliverables.



What You'll Be Doing


This is a specialist paid search role with real autonomy and line management responsibility. You'll be owning the day-to-day management and strategy of Google Ads and Microsoft Ads campaigns across a portfolio of iGaming clients — working with a high degree of independence while collaborating closely with the Senior Paid Search Manager on planning and client development. You'll also own iGaming compliance for your accounts and manage up to two direct reports, so the ability to lead as well as deliver is essential.
In practice, that looks like:

  • Owning day-to-day management and optimisation of Paid Search campaigns across Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, and associated display and performance formats
  • Conducting daily account checks to identify issues and opportunities — acting on findings promptly before clients notice them
  • Monitoring spend and performance against client KPIs — escalating risks early, never sitting on them

As an Engagement Manager within Customer Excellence and Professional Services at Smartsheet, you will play a critical role in setting customers up for success by prescriptively crafting and then leading the execution of large and transformative enterprise projects for our most strategic customers. The Engagement Manager serves as a trusted advisor to Smartsheet customers, provides mentorship to Sales & Professional Services teams, drives alignment across each customer’s projects, and ensures the highest customer satisfaction levels.

Partnered with the Account Team, Services Sales, and Service Delivery, the Engagement Manager contributes to pre-sales scoping and discovery activities, acting as a conduit across the organization to develop and articulate comprehensive implementation proposals. The Engagement Manager will then maintain the executive relationships and act as a critical issue point within these implementations in a billable capacity, ensuring tight customer alignment and offering proactive and prescriptive advice resulting in outstanding Customer Success.

As the Engagement Manager, you will manage several projects/programs concurrently spanning 1 or more Large Enterprise customers. Engagement managers will have a targeted utilization rate, be responsible for the development of best practices, and will manage business processes.

You will report to the Manager of Engagement Delivery, this is a remote eligible position and you may work remotely from anywhere in the US where Smartsheet is registered

You Will:

  • Contribute to the development and ownership of the Smartsheet Delivery Methodology and Professional Services PMO function
  • Contribute to engagement delivery standard operating procedures (SOPs)

  • Liaison with necessary teams within Smartsheet to achieve the above items
  • Other duties as assigned

You Have:

  • 4+ years of experience in customer-facing positions in a professional capacity ideally at Software or SaaS Provider
  • At least 2 years of Project and Program Management experience at the enterprise level
  • 2+ years of experience, leading customer-facing engagements in the enterprise space
  • Management of large billable projects for external customers
  • Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Claude) to accelerate drafting, analysis, and process design, with sound judgment on accuracy, confidentiality, and customer data handling.

At Smartsheet, your ideas are heard, your potential is supported, and your contributions have real impact. You’ll have the freedom to explore, push boundaries, and grow beyond your role. Job Description Summary:


Position Title: Director, Franchise Operations Swire SOUTH

Department: Franchise Leadership, Mountain Arctic Pacific USA (aka Swire & Mainstream)

Reports To: Senior Director, Franchise Operations - Swire

Location: Phoenix, Arizona


POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Director of Franchise Operations is a pivotal role responsible for the strategic oversight and leadership within an assigned geographical and bottler territory(ies). This leader will serve as the 360-degree 'face of KO’ to the bottler head in the assigned geography, ensuring alignment and delivery of the Annual Business Plan (ABP), while driving performance across topline, share, volume, and other key objectives. This role necessitates proactive an effective focus on driving execution with bottling partners, performance forecasting with as-needed planning adjustments, execution of controllables, and stewardship to accelerate and ensure key support functions' needs are met. Responsibilities are for the total KO portfolio.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a dynamic leader to further Coca-Cola's growth and reputation in the assigned geography, embodying the company’s values and commitment to excellence.

What You’ll Do for Us

1. Strategic Leadership:

- Act as the primary point of contact and 'face of KO' to the bottler head in the assigned geography.

- Develop and implement strategic plans in alignment with corporate goals to ensure the annual business plan (ABP) is delivered effectively.

- Drive and support bottler strategies for topline, share, volume, and other key objectives.

2. Performance Management:

- Establish and forecast performance metrics, adjusting plans as necessary to meet objectives.

- Analyze market trends, consumer insights, and competitor activities to inform strategies and optimize performance.

3. Operational Execution:

- Ensure execution controllables are in place to drive efficiently toward established goals.

- Identify gaps in performance and implement corrective actions with urgency as needed.

4. Stewardship and Support Function Leadership:

- Ensure the acceleration of key support functions, facilitating collaboration and engagement among cross-functional teams.

- Provide leadership in ensuring that all support functions have the necessary resources and guidance to meet their objectives.

5. Relationship Building:

- Cultivate strong relationships with bottlers, stakeholders, and partners to drive alignment and cooperation.

- Represent Coca-Cola values in all interactions, promoting transparency, integrity, and ethical leadership.

6. Innovation and Continuous Improvement:

- Encourage and pioneer innovative approaches to franchise leadership and operations.

- Promote a culture of continuous learning and improvement within the territory.

7. Other projects tied to strategic priorities as may be identified according to business need.

Requirements & Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Marketing, or related field; MBA preferred.

- Minimum of 10 years of experience in franchise operations or a similar leadership role within the CPG industry.

- Proven track record of delivering strategic objectives related to topline, share, and volume.

- Strong analytical, forecasting, and strategic planning skills.

- Excellent interpersonal, communication, and leadership skills.

- Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment and adapt to changing circumstances.

Values & Behaviors Expected:

- Leadership & Integrity: Demonstrate ethical leadership and integrity in all business dealings.

- Collaboration: Foster teamwork and collaboration across functions and territories.

- Diversity & Inclusion: Champion a culture of respect for diversity and inclusion.

- Innovation: Encourage innovation and forward-thinking solutions.

- Accountability: Take ownership and accountability for results and actions.

What We’ll Do for You

  • Enable you to lead complex system initiatives that reshape how Coca‑Cola competes in market and builds future growth capabilities across our bottling partners.
  • Provide scope to apply transformation leadership that bridges strategic thinking and market execution within a collaborative, growth-oriented environment.
  • Offer opportunities to build and enhance system capabilities that make our franchise network more agile, data-enabled, and efficient.
  • Support your development as a transformation leader through exposure to regional and enterprise-level challenges that strengthen long-term business readiness.
All persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form (Form I-9) upon hire.

Annual Business Planning, Business Plan Implementation, Capacity Planning, Channels Strategy, Contract Management, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), Distribution Operations Management, Financial Performance Management, Negotiation, Strategic Leadership, Teamwork

30

We are taking deliberate action to nurture an inclusive culture that is grounded in our company purpose, to refresh the world and make a difference. We act with a growth mindset, take an expansive approach to what’s possible and believe in continuous learning to improve our business and ourselves. We focus on four key behaviors – curious, empowered, inclusive and agile – and value how we work as much as what we achieve. We believe that our culture is one of the reasons our company continues to thrive after 130+ years. Visit Our Purpose and Vision to learn more about these behaviors and how you can bring them to life in your next role at Coca-Cola.

About Gruve

Gruve is an innovative software services startup dedicated to transforming enterprises to AI powerhouses. We specialize in cybersecurity, customer experience, cloud infrastructure, and advanced technologies such as Large Language Models (LLMs). Our mission is to assist our customers in their business strategies utilizing their data to make more intelligent decisions. As a well-funded early-stage startup, Gruve offers a dynamic environment with strong customer and partner networks.

Position summary:

We are looking for a proactive L1 System Administrator to support day-to-day Microsoft Defender operations. The role is responsible for monitoring security alerts, performing initial triage, validating endpoint protection status, logging incidents and escalating potential threats to L2/L3 teams. The administrator will follow approved security procedures and runbooks to support timely incident response and continuous security monitoring.

Key Responsibilities:

Microsoft Defender Monitoring

  • Monitor Microsoft Defender portals, security dashboards, alerts and incident queues.
  • Perform initial triage of malware detections, suspicious activities and endpoint security alerts.
  • Review alert details, device information, severity and timestamps to assess potential impact.
  • Perform basic checks on Defender sensor health, endpoint onboarding and protection status.
  • Identify endpoints with failed scans, outdated security intelligence or protection-related issues.
  • Escalate suspicious activities and high-severity alerts according to established procedures.

Security Incident & Endpoint Support

  • Create, categorize, prioritize and update security incident tickets in ServiceNow or equivalent ITSM tools.
  • Collect relevant alert evidence, device details, timestamps and investigation information.
  • Perform approved first-level checks using documented security runbooks.
  • Track incidents and coordinate with L2/SOC teams for investigation and remediation.
  • Validate remediation status and endpoint protection recovery as directed.
  • Avoid unauthorized containment or remediation actions and follow established security escalation procedures.

Operations & Service Management

  • Follow Security Incident, Incident, Change and Request Management processes.
  • Ensure timely alert acknowledgement, escalation and SLA compliance.
  • Maintain accurate incident records, operational checklists and shift handover documentation.
  • Coordinate with L2/L3, SOC, Endpoint, Identity and Infrastructure teams.
  • Support routine security reporting, alert tracking and operational reviews.
  • Identify recurring alerts and report monitoring or documentation gaps to L2.
  • Ensure effective APAC–EMEA–NLAM shift handovers and uninterrupted 24x7 monitoring.

Required Skills & Qualifications:

  • 1–3 years of experience in IT operations, security monitoring, endpoint support or security incident management.
  • Basic understanding of endpoint security, antivirus, malware detection and security alerts.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint or equivalent endpoint protection tools.
  • Basic knowledge of Windows operating systems, processes and endpoint health.
  • Ability to review alerts, capture evidence and follow documented investigation procedures.
  • Understanding of incident severity, escalation matrices and SLA requirements.
  • Familiarity with ServiceNow or equivalent ITSM platforms.
  • Good communication, documentation and shift handover skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and adherence to security procedures.
  • Willingness to work in rotational shifts in a 24x7 security operations environment.

Preferred Skills & Qualifications:

  • Microsoft SC-900 or equivalent security fundamentals certification.
  • Basic knowledge of Microsoft Defender XDR and Microsoft Sentinel.
  • Familiarity with malware, phishing, endpoint threats and common attack techniques.
  • Basic PowerShell and Windows troubleshooting knowledge.
  • Exposure to KQL, security dashboards and incident reporting.
  • Understanding of ITIL and security incident management processes.
  • Security Monitoring | Microsoft Defender | Alert Triage | Endpoint Protection | Basic Threat Analysis.
  • Incident Logging | Evidence Collection | Runbook Execution | SLA Compliance.
  • Escalation Management | Shift Handover | Global 24x7 Operations

Why Gruve

At Gruve, we foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive and contribute their best work. If you’re passionate about technology and eager to make an impact, we’d love to hear from you.

Gruve is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and thank all who apply; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

raw.description:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

Enterprise Account Executive

As an Account Executive at Quince, you will be responsible for developing, managing, and growing a portfolio of enterprise merchandise clients across industries including Finance, Legal, Sports, Media, and Entertainment. This role requires a proactive and strategic approach to business development, relationship management, and ability to operate in a fast-paced dynamic start up environment. Commission is uncapped, and top performers are rewarded accordingly. You will have a deep understanding of Quince's product offerings and be able to represent the brand and drive meaningful sales growth across a variety of customers and industries.

Responsibilities

  • Develop, manage, and grow your own book of business
  • Promote Quince to prospective and existing enterprise clients through a variety of outreach opportunities
  • Leverage existing relationships with companies and distributors to drive large volume sales and manage both existing and new project opportunities
  • Effectively represent Quince through outstanding product knowledge and outstanding service
  • Proactively seek opportunities for creative expansion within the segment
  • Maintain/track your business pipeline in HubSpot and Sales Navigator

Qualifications

Required:

  • 5+ years of Corporate or B2B sales experience with enterprise-level business
  • Proven track record of generating a book of business & driving sales growth
  • Proven track record of successfully identifying, developing, negotiating, and closing opportunities at Enterprise level
  • Proven track record of successfully positioning and selling solutions to new and existing customers and market segments
  • Proficiency in CRM tools such as LinkedIn Sales Navigator
  • Outside-of-the-box thinker who is motivated by results
  • Entrepreneurial attitude and an ability to work independently and competitively in a fast-paced, startup environment
  • Excellent proactive, solution oriented, problem-solving skills and flexibility
  • Strong verbal and written communication with demonstrated ability to communicate effectively
  • Proficiency in Google Workspace

Preferred:

  • Experience in corporate gifting sales such as ASI, PPAI
  • Knowledge of print, promotional, and apparel industries

Posted range is reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location.

$80,000—$120,000 USD

Posted range is reflective of total On-Target Earnings (OTE) and may vary depending upon experience level and location. Equity may also be provided for eligible roles.

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY
